excerpt: A cabin-style cedar sauna for 2–4 with two-tier benches, a 9kW heater and everything needed included.
description:
The Henley is the cabin shape in the range: a sloped roofline and plain elevation that sits beside a deck or patio without demanding attention. Inside, benches are stacked on two tiers, which is the detail that matters in use — the upper bench runs hot and the lower sits cooler, so you move down rather than get out when a session gets long.
Heat comes from a 9kW electric heater, which reaches temperature roughly 50% faster than the 6kW units commonly fitted at this size. On a winter evening that is the difference between waiting and using it.
Construction is cedar tongue-and-groove with an 8mm tempered glass door and a powder-coated galvanised steel roof. Everything needed arrives with it: heater, stones, Wi-Fi control panel, bucket, ladle, LED lighting and hooks. Components are ready to assemble with step-by-step guidance in a companion app.

excerpt: A traditional cedar barrel sauna for 2–4 with facing linear benches and a 9kW heater, fully equipped.
description:
The Paxton is the barrel — the shape most people picture when they think of a sauna, and the one with the longest history behind it. Two linear benches face each other in the classic Finnish arrangement, so two people sit across from one another or one person lies out along a bench.
The curved cedar wall is not only styling: it puts less volume above head height than a square room, so the air a heater has to warm is smaller. A 9kW electric heater reaches temperature roughly 50% faster than the 6kW units commonly fitted at this size.
Construction is cedar tongue-and-groove with an 8mm tempered glass door and a powder-coated galvanised steel roof over the curve. Heater, stones, Wi-Fi control panel, bucket, ladle, LED lighting and hooks are included from day one, and the components assemble with step-by-step guidance in a companion app.

excerpt: A 2-person indoor infrared sauna with tinted glass, eight low-EMF panels, red light and chromotherapy.
description:
The Knox is an indoor infrared cabin, and the tinted 8mm tempered glass is the reason it works in a shared room. Clear glass in an open-plan space makes a sauna a spectacle; tinted glass keeps the heat in and gives you somewhere private to sit even when the room around it is in use.
Eight low-EMF far infrared carbon panels surround the bench and reach working temperature around 20% faster than fewer, larger emitters — infrared heats the body rather than the air, so panel placement matters more than raw wattage.
The cabin uses cedar panels 33% thicker than standard with double-wall construction, which is what holds the heat in a room that is not insulated like a sauna building. Red light therapy, chromotherapy, Bluetooth speakers and the controls are all included. Panels arrive pre-built, pre-drilled, pre-stained and pre-wired.
